name: Silverguard
note: Sizes and offsets are in HERO WORLD units and were measured in tools/blender/fit_gear.py against the profile of the body at the height each piece sits, not against bounding boxes. The shield is still the Tier 2 Ironwood one; the ladder does not call for a new shield at Tier 3.

items.name: helmet
items.why: 0.50 wide clears the skull's 0.444 at ear level (z 1.259). The Z squash to 0.857 is what makes it fit at all: at natural proportions the arch apex lands at z 1.32, below his eyes at 1.33. Squashed, the apex sits at 1.360 and the crown at 1.540, just over the head's 1.500.

items.name: shoulderR
items.why: The SAME mesh as the left, mirrored by a negative X scale rather than generated twice. That saved a 15-credit generation and makes the pair symmetric by construction. A negative scale inverts winding order; it is safe here only because the material is doubleSided, which was checked in the GLB rather than assumed.

items.name: sword
items.why: 0.60 against the Ironwood sword's 0.47, so it reads as 0.400 of his height rather than 0.313. anchor 'grip' is load-bearing: the RightHand bone HEAD is the wrist, and anchoring there left the grip 0.0893 short of the palm with the crossguard lying across the forearm. The 90 degree Z rotation turns the guard front-to-back so it no longer spans the arm, dropping the sword's x-extent from 0.199 to 0.064.

items.name: shield
items.why: anchor 'grip' moves it 0.0836 out to the palm. The same wrist-not-palm error affected the shield from Tier 2 onward; it was simply less visible on a disc than on a crossguard.
